q: Corton-Charlemagne produces wine of which colour?
exp: The white Grand Cru of the Corton hill, traditionally said to have been planted at the emperor's wish so his beard would not be stained.

q: Which Grand Cru of Chambolle-Musigny produces a small quantity of white wine?
exp: Musigny Blanc is made in tiny volumes and is the only white permitted from a Cote de Nuits Grand Cru.

q: Clos de Vougeot's reputation for variable quality is usually attributed to what?
opts: A rule against new oak barrels
Its planting of Gamay alongside Pinot Noir
exp: Fifty hectares walled as one by monks who blended it all. Divided now among dozens of owners, across ground that slopes unevenly, it can no longer be one wine.

q: Which order of monks did most to map and wall Burgundy's vineyards in the Middle Ages?
exp: Cistercian and Benedictine houses worked the land for centuries and recorded which parcels ripened differently. The climat map is largely their survey.

q: Echezeaux and Grands-Echezeaux lie within which commune?
exp: Flagey-Echezeaux's village wine is sold as Vosne-Romanee, which is one of Burgundy's more confusing administrative arrangements.

q: Which soil type underlies the finest Chablis vineyards?
opts: Granite with a thin sandy topsoil
exp: A Jurassic seabed of limestone and marl, full of fossilised oyster shells. The Grands Crus and best Premiers Crus sit on it, and Petit Chablis largely does not.

q: How many Grand Cru climats does Chablis have?
exp: Blanchot, Bougros, Les Clos, Grenouilles, Les Preuses, Valmur and Vaudesir, all on one south-west facing slope above the town.

q: Chablis is defined stylistically by which pair of qualities?
opts: High acidity and little or no new oak
exp: The cool site gives the acidity; the house style debate is over how much oak, with many producers using none at all.

q: Petit Chablis differs from Chablis chiefly in what respect?
opts: It must be aged in oak before release
exp: A separate appellation for outlying sites off the Kimmeridgian, on the younger Portlandian rock above it, generally lighter and for earlier drinking.

q: Which Chablis Grand Cru climat is often singled out as the most structured and longest-lived?
exp: Les Clos is the largest and most celebrated of the seven. Montee de Tonnerre and Fourchaume are Premiers Crus, and fine ones.

q: Rully, Givry and Montagny sit in the Cote Chalonnaise. Which neighbour outsizes them all?
exp: Mercurey is predominantly red and the best known of the four village appellations there.

q: Montagny is unusual among Cote Chalonnaise appellations because it produces what?
exp: Chardonnay alone. Rully makes both and is also a centre for Cremant de Bourgogne.

q: Pouilly-Fuisse is found in which sub-region?
exp: The best-known white appellation of the Maconnais, beneath the rock of Solutre, and the first there to gain Premier Cru status.

q: Bouzeron holds a village appellation for which grape?
exp: The only village appellation in Burgundy dedicated to Aligote, and the strongest argument that the grape can be more than a kir base.

q: What distinguishes Cremant de Bourgogne from a tank-method sparkling wine?
opts: It is fermented under pressure in tank
Its second fermentation is in the bottle
exp: Bottle-fermented from Burgundian grapes, with minimum ageing on lees set by the appellation.

q: Fleurie, Morgon and Moulin-a-Vent are three of the Beaujolais crus. How many exist in all?
exp: Brouilly, Cote de Brouilly, Chenas, Chiroubles, Fleurie, Julienas, Morgon, Moulin-a-Vent, Regnie and Saint-Amour, each labelled by its own name.
